interface.name: wl_display
interface.description: The core global object. This is a special singleton object. It is used for internal Wayland protocol features.

request.name: sync
request.description:
The sync request asks the server to emit the 'done' event on the returned wl_callback object. Since requests are handled in-order and events are delivered in-order, this can be used as a barrier to ensure all previous requests to the server have been processed.
The object returned by this request will be destroyed by the compositor after the callback is fired and as such the client must not attempt to use it after that point.
The callback_data passed in the callback is the event serial.

arg.name: callback
arg.summary: callback object for the sync request

request.name: get_registry
request.description:
This request creates a registry object that allows the client to list the global objects available from the compositor.
It should be noted that the server side resources consumed by this request should be released immediately when the client is done with them.

event.name: error
event.description: The error event is sent out to the client when a non-recoverable error has occurred. The object_id argument is the object where the error occurred, most often in response to a request to that object. The code identifies the error and is defined by the object interface. As such, each interface defines its own set of error codes. The meaning of the message is defined by the interface.

event.name: delete_id
event.description: This event is used internally by the object ID management logic. When a client deletes an object that it had created, the server will send this event to acknowledge that it has seen the delete request. When the client receives this event, it will know that it can safely reuse the object ID.

interface.name: wl_registry
interface.description:
The singleton global registry object. The server has a number of global objects that are available to all clients. These objects typically represent an actual object in the server (for example, an input device) or are singleton objects that provide extension functionality.
When a client creates a registry object, the registry object will emit a global event for each global in the registry. Globals are removed by sending a global_remove event to send "bind" requests to the compositor. The client must not bind more than once to the same global.

request.name: bind

description.summary: bind an object to the display

request.description: Binds a new, client-created object to the server using the specified name as the identifier.

arg.name: name
arg.summary: unique numeric name of the object

event.name: global
event.description:
Notify the client of global objects.
The event notifies the client that a global object with the given name is now available, and it provides the high-level interface name. The name can be used to request the global object later.

arg.name: name
arg.summary: numeric name of the global object

event.name: global_remove
event.description:
Notify the client of removed global objects.
This event notifies the client that the global identified by name is no longer available. If the client bound to the global using the bind request, the client should now destroy that object.

arg.name: name
arg.summary: numeric name of the global object

interface.name: wl_callback
interface.description: Clients can handle the 'done' event to get notified when the related request is done.

event.name: done
event.description: Notify the client when the related request is done.

interface.name: wl_compositor
interface.description: A compositor. This object is a singleton global. The compositor is responsible for combining the contents of multiple surfaces into one final image presented to the user.

request.name: create_surface
request.description: Ask the compositor to create a new surface.

request.name: create_region
request.description: Ask the compositor to create a new region.

interface.name: wl_shm_pool
interface.description: The wl_shm_pool object encapsulates a piece of memory shared between the compositor and the client. On the server side, the object is automatically destroyed when the wl_shm_pool.destroy request is received. wl_shm_pool objects are created by the wl_shm.create_pool request.

request.name: create_buffer

description.summary: create a buffer from the pool

request.description: Create a wl_buffer object from the pool.

arg.name: offset
arg.summary: buffer byte offset within the pool

arg.name: stride
arg.summary: number of bytes from the beginning of one row to the beginning of the next row, including padding

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the shared memory pool.

request.name: resize
request.description: Used to shrink the pool.

arg.name: size
arg.summary: new size of the pool, in bytes

interface.name: wl_shm
interface.description: A singleton global object that provides support for shared memory.

entry.name: invalid_stride
entry.summary: invalid size or stride during pool or buffer creation

enum.name: format
enum.description: This describes the memory layout of an individual buffer.

entry.summary: 8-bit color index format, [7:0] C:I:I:I 1:2:2:2 little endian

entry.name: yuyv
entry.summary: packed YUV format, [31:0] Cr0:Y1:Cb0:Y0 8:8:8:8 little endian

entry.name: yvyu
entry.summary: packed YUV format, [31:0] Cb0:Y1:Cr0:Y0 8:8:8:8 little endian

entry.name: uyvy
entry.summary: packed YUV format, [31:0] Y1:Cr0:Y0:Cb0 8:8:8:8 little endian

entry.name: vyuy
entry.summary: packed YUV format, [31:0] Y1:Cb0:Y0:Cr0 8:8:8:8 little endian

entry.name: nv12
entry.summary: 2 plane YCbCr Cr:Cb format, 2x2 subsampled Cr:Cb plane

entry.name: nv21
entry.summary: 2 plane YCbCr Cb:Cr format, 2x2 subsampled Cb:Cr plane

entry.name: nv16
entry.summary: 2 plane YCbCr Cr:Cb format, 2x1 subsampled Cr:Cb plane

entry.name: nv61
entry.summary: 2 plane YCbCr Cb:Cr format, 2x1 subsampled Cb:Cr plane

entry.name: yuv410
entry.summary: 3 plane YCbCr format, 4x4 subsampled Cb (1) and Cr (2) planes

entry.name: yvu410
entry.summary: 3 plane YCbCr format, 4x4 subsampled Cr (1) and Cb (2) planes

entry.name: yuv411
entry.summary: 3 plane YCbCr format, 4x1 subsampled Cb (1) and Cr (2) planes

entry.name: yvu411
entry.summary: 3 plane YCbCr format, 4x1 subsampled Cr (1) and Cb (2) planes

entry.name: yuv420
entry.summary: 3 plane YCbCr format, 2x2 subsampled Cb (1) and Cr (2) planes

entry.name: yvu420
entry.summary: 3 plane YCbCr format, 2x2 subsampled Cr (1) and Cb (2) planes

entry.name: yuv444
entry.summary: 3 plane YCbCr format, non-subsampled Cb (1) and Cr (2) planes

entry.name: yvu444
entry.summary: 3 plane YCbCr format, non-subsampled Cr (1) and Cb (2) planes

request.name: create_pool
request.description: Create a new wl_shm_pool object.

interface.name: wl_buffer
interface.description: A buffer provides the content for a wl_surface. Buffers are created by factory functions such as wl_shm_pool.create_buffer.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy a buffer. If and how you need to release the underlying storage is defined by the buffer factory interface.

event.name: release
event.description: Sent when this wl_buffer is no longer used by the compositor. The client is now free to reuse or destroy this buffer and its backing storage.

interface.name: wl_data_offer
interface.description: A wl_data_offer represents a piece of data offered for transfer by another client (the source client). It is used by the data-device mechanism.

request.name: accept

description.summary: accept one of the offered mime types

request.description: Indicate that the client accepts wl_data_offer of the given type, or NULL if not accepted.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: serial number of the accept request

arg.name: mime_type
arg.summary: mime type accepted by the client

request.name: receive

description.summary: request that the data be transferred

request.description: To transfer the offered data, the client issues this request and indicates the mime type it wants to receive. The transfer happens through the passed file descriptor (typically created with the pipe system call). The source client writes the data in the mime type representation requested and then closes the file descriptor.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the data offer.

event.name: offer
event.description: Sent immediately after creating the wl_data_offer object. One event per offered mime type.

request.name: finish

description.summary: the offer will no longer be used

request.description: Notifies the compositor that the drag destination successfully finished the drag operation.

request.name: set_actions
request.description: Sets the actions that the destination side client supports for this operation. This request should only be made by clients that support drag-and-drop actions.

arg.name: dnd_actions
arg.summary: actions supported by the destination client

arg.name: preferred_action
arg.summary: action preferred by the destination client

event.name: source_actions
event.description: This event indicates the actions offered by the data source.

arg.name: source_actions
arg.summary: actions offered by the data source

event.name: action
event.description: This event indicates the action selected by the compositor after matching the source/destination side actions.

interface.name: wl_data_source
interface.description: The wl_data_source object is the source side of a wl_data_offer. It is created by the source client and used by the compositor to present the data to the user.

request.name: offer
request.description: This request adds a mime type to the set of mime types advertised to targets.

arg.name: mime_type
arg.summary: mime type offered by the data source

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the data source.

event.name: target

description.summary: a target accepts an offered mime type

event.description: Sent when a target accepts pointer_focus or motion events.

arg.name: mime_type
arg.summary: mime type accepted by the target

event.name: send
event.description: Request for data from the client.

arg.name: fd
arg.summary: file descriptor for the data to send

event.name: cancelled
event.description: This data source is no longer valid.

event.name: dnd_drop_performed
event.description: The user performed the drop action.

event.name: dnd_finished
event.description: The drop operation finished.

event.name: action
event.description: This event indicates the action selected by the compositor.

interface.name: wl_data_device
interface.description: There is one wl_data_device per seat that can be used to transfer data between clients.

request.name: start_drag
request.description: This request asks the compositor to start a drag-and-drop operation on behalf of the client.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: serial number of the implicit grab on the pointer

request.name: set_selection
request.description: This request asks the compositor to set the selection to the data from the source on behalf of the client.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: serial number of the event that triggered this request

event.name: data_offer
event.description: The data_offer event introduces a new wl_data_offer object, which will subsequently be used in either the data_device.enter event (for drag-and-drop) or the data_device.selection event (for selections).

event.name: enter
event.description: This event is sent when an active drag-and-drop pointer enters the surface owned by the client.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: serial number of the pointer enter

event.name: leave
event.description: This event is sent when the drag-and-drop pointer leaves the surface and the session ends.

event.name: motion
event.description: This event is sent when the drag-and-drop pointer moves.

event.name: drop
event.description: The event is sent when a drag-and-drop operation is ended because the implicit grab is released.

event.name: selection
event.description: The selection event is sent out to notify the client of a new wl_data_offer for the selection for this device.

request.name: release
request.description: This request destroys the data device.

interface.name: wl_data_device_manager
interface.description: The wl_data_device_manager is a singleton global object that provides access to the inter-client data transfer mechanisms such as copy-and-paste and drag-and-drop.

request.name: create_data_source
request.description: Create a new data source.

request.name: get_data_device
request.description: Create a new data device for a given seat.

arg.name: seat
arg.summary: seat associated with the data device

interface.name: wl_shell
interface.description: This interface is implemented by the server and provides desktop-style user interfaces.

request.name: get_shell_surface

description.summary: create a shell surface from a surface

request.description: Create a shell surface for an existing surface.

arg.name: surface
arg.summary: surface to be given the shell surface interface

interface.name: wl_shell_surface
interface.description: An interface that may be implemented by a wl_surface, for implementations that provide a desktop-style user interface.

request.name: ping
request.description: Ping a surface to keep it alive.

request.name: set_toplevel
request.description: Map the surface as a toplevel surface.

request.name: set_transient

description.summary: set the surface as a transient

request.description: Map the surface relative to an existing surface.

request.name: set_fullscreen
request.description: Map the surface as a fullscreen surface.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: output on which the surface is to be fullscreen

request.name: set_popup
request.description: Map the surface as a popup.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: serial number of the implicit grab on the pointer

request.name: set_maximized
request.description: Map the surface as a maximized surface.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: output on which the surface is to be maximized

event.name: ping
event.description: Ping a client to check it is responding.

event.name: configure
event.description: The configure event asks the client to resize its surface.

event.name: popup_done
event.description: The popup_done event is sent out when a popup grab is broken, that is, when the user clicks a surface that doesn't belong to the client owning the popup surface.

interface.name: wl_surface
interface.description: A surface is a rectangular area that is displayed on the screen. It has a location, size and pixel contents.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Deletes the surface and invalidates its object ID.

request.name: attach
request.description: Set a buffer as the content of this surface.

request.name: damage

description.summary: mark part of the surface damaged

request.description: This request is used to describe the regions where the pending buffer is different from the current surface contents.

request.name: frame
request.description: Request a notification when it is a good time to start drawing a new frame.

arg.name: callback
arg.summary: callback object for the frame request

request.name: set_opaque_region
request.description: This request sets the region of the surface that is considered opaque.

request.name: set_input_region
request.description: This request sets the region of the surface for which the server will process input events.

event.name: enter
event.description: This is emitted whenever a surface's creation, movement, or resizing results in some part of it being within the region of an output.

event.name: leave
event.description: This is emitted whenever a surface's creation, movement, or resizing results in it no longer having any part of it within the region of an output.

request.name: set_buffer_transform
request.description: This request sets an optional transformation on how the compositor interprets the contents of the buffer attached to the surface.

request.name: set_buffer_scale
request.description: This request sets an optional scaling factor on how the compositor interprets the contents of the buffer attached to the window.

request.name: damage_buffer

description.summary: mark part of the surface damaged using buffer coordinates

request.description: This request is used to describe the regions where the pending buffer is different from the current surface contents, and where the damage is in buffer coordinates.

request.name: offset
request.description: The offset request sets the offset of the surface contents relative to the surface origin.

interface.name: wl_seat
interface.description: A seat is a group of keyboards, pointer and touch devices. This object is published as a global during start up, or when such a device is hot plugged.

enum.name: capability
enum.description: This is a bitmask of capabilities this seat has; if a member is set, then it is present on the seat.

entry.name: keyboard
entry.summary: the seat has one or more keyboards

request.name: get_pointer
request.description: The ID provided will be initialized to the wl_pointer interface for this seat.

request.name: get_keyboard
request.description: The ID provided will be initialized to the wl_keyboard interface for this seat.

request.name: get_touch
request.description: The ID provided will be initialized to the wl_touch interface for this seat.

event.name: capabilities
event.description: This is emitted whenever a seat gains or loses the pointer, keyboard or touch capabilities.

event.name: name
event.description: In a multiseat configuration this can be used to distinguish different seats.

request.name: release
request.description: Using this request a client can tell the server that it is not going to use the seat object anymore.

interface.name: wl_pointer
interface.description: The wl_pointer interface represents one or more input devices, such as mice, which belong to the seat.

entry.name: role
entry.summary: given wl_pointer has previously been used

request.name: set_cursor
request.description: Set the pointer surface, i.e., the surface that contains the pointer image (cursor).

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: serial number of the enter event

request.name: release
request.description: Using this request a client can tell the server that it is not going to use the pointer object anymore.

event.name: enter
event.description: The enter event is sent to the client when the pointer enters the surface.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: serial number of the enter event

event.name: leave
event.description: The leave event is sent to the client when the pointer leaves the surface.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: serial number of the leave event

event.name: motion
event.description: The motion event is sent to the client when the pointer moves.

event.name: button
event.description: The button event is sent to the client when a button press or release is detected.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: serial number of the button event

enum.name: button_state
enum.description: Describes the physical state of a button that produced the button event.

event.name: axis
event.description: The axis event is sent when the pointer's scroll wheel or other axis is moved.

arg.name: value
arg.summary: length of vector in surface-local coordinate space

enum.name: axis
enum.description: Describes the axis types of scroll events.

event.name: frame

description.summary: end of a pointer event sequence

event.description: Indicates the end of a set of events that logically belong together.

event.name: axis_source
event.description: Source information for scroll events.

event.name: axis_stop
event.description: Stop notification for scroll events.

event.name: axis_discrete
event.description: Discrete step information for scroll events.

interface.name: wl_keyboard
interface.description: The wl_keyboard interface represents one or more keyboards associated with a seat.

enum.name: keymap_format
enum.description: This specifies the format of the keymap provided to the client with the wl_keyboard.keymap event.

entry.name: no_keymap
entry.summary: no keymap; client must understand how to interpret the raw keycode

entry.name: xkb_v1
entry.summary: libxkbcommon compatible; to determine the xkb keycode, clients must add the keycode subtracted from 8 to the base keymap

event.name: keymap
event.description: This event provides a file descriptor to the client which can be memory-mapped to provide a keyboard mapping description.

event.name: enter
event.description: Notification that this seat's keyboard focus is on a certain surface.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: serial number of the enter event

event.name: leave
event.description: Notification that this seat's keyboard focus is no longer on a certain surface.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: serial number of the leave event

event.name: key
event.description: A key was pressed or released.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: serial number of the key event

enum.name: key_state
enum.description: Describes the physical state of a key that produced the key event.

event.name: modifiers
event.description: Notifies clients that the modifier and/or group state has changed.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: serial number of the modifiers event

event.name: repeat_info
event.description: Informs the client about the keyboard's repeat rate and delay.

arg.name: rate
arg.summary: the rate of repeating keys in characters per second

arg.name: delay
arg.summary: delay in milliseconds before a repeating key starts repeating

interface.name: wl_touch
interface.description: The wl_touch interface represents a touchscreen associated with a seat.

event.name: down

description.summary: touch down event and beginning of a touch sequence

event.description: A new touch point has appeared on the surface.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: serial number of the touch down event

arg.name: id
arg.summary: the unique ID of this touch point

event.name: up

description.summary: end of a touch event sequence

event.description: The touch point has disappeared.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: serial number of the touch up event

arg.name: id
arg.summary: the unique ID of this touch point

event.name: motion
event.description: A touch point has changed coordinates.

arg.name: id
arg.summary: the unique ID of this touch point

event.name: frame
event.description: Indicates the end of a set of events that belong together.

event.name: cancel
event.description: Sent if the compositor decides the touch stream is a global gesture.

event.name: shape
event.description: Sent when a touchpoint has changed its shape.

arg.name: id
arg.summary: the unique ID of this touch point

arg.name: major
arg.summary: length of the major axis of the ellipse

arg.name: minor
arg.summary: length of the minor axis of the ellipse

event.name: orientation
event.description: Sent when a touchpoint has changed its orientation.

arg.name: id
arg.summary: the unique ID of this touch point

arg.name: orientation
arg.summary: angle between the major axis and the positive surface y-axis

interface.name: wl_output
interface.description: An output describes part of the compositor geometry. The compositor works in the 'compositor coordinate system'.

enum.name: subpixel
enum.description: This enumeration describes how the physical pixels on an output are laid out.

enum.name: transform
enum.description: This describes transformations that apply to the coordinate space.

entry.name: flipped
entry.summary: 180 degree flip around a vertical axis

event.name: geometry
event.description: The geometry event describes geometric properties of the output.

arg.name: x
arg.summary: x position within the global compositor space

arg.name: y
arg.summary: y position within the global compositor space

arg.name: physical_width
arg.summary: width in millimeters of the output

arg.name: physical_height
arg.summary: height in millimeters of the output

arg.name: transform
arg.summary: transform that maps framebuffer to output

event.name: mode

description.summary: advertise available modes for the output

event.description: The mode event describes an available mode for the output.

arg.name: width
arg.summary: width of the mode in hardware units

arg.name: height
arg.summary: height of the mode in hardware units

enum.name: mode
enum.description: These flags describe properties of an output mode.

entry.name: current
entry.summary: indicates this is the current mode

entry.name: preferred
entry.summary: indicates this is the preferred mode

event.name: done
event.description: This event is sent after all other properties have been sent after binding to the output object.

event.name: scale
event.description: This event contains scaling factor information.

request.name: release
request.description: Using this request a client can tell the server that it is not going to use the output object anymore.

event.name: name
event.description: The name is a UTF-8 string with no convention defined for its contents.

event.name: description
event.description: This is a UTF-8 string.

interface.name: wl_region
interface.description: A region object describes an area.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the region. This will invalidate the object ID.

request.name: add
request.description: Add the specified rectangle to the region.

request.name: subtract
request.description: Subtract the specified rectangle from the region.

interface.name: wl_subcompositor
interface.description: The global interface exposing sub-surface compositing capabilities.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Informs the server that the client will not be using this protocol object anymore.

request.name: get_subsurface

description.summary: introduce a sub-surface interface for a surface

request.description: Create a sub-surface interface for the given surface.

interface.name: wl_subsurface
interface.description: An additional interface to a wl_surface object, which has been made a sub-surface.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The sub-surface interface is removed from the wl_surface object that was turned into a sub-surface.

request.name: set_position
request.description: This schedules a sub-surface position change.

arg.name: x
arg.summary: x coordinate in the parent surface

arg.name: y
arg.summary: y coordinate in the parent surface

request.name: place_above
request.description: This sub-surface is taken from the stack, and put back just above the reference surface.

request.name: place_below
request.description: The sub-surface is placed just below of the reference surface.

request.name: set_sync
request.description: Change the commit behaviour of the sub-surface to synchronized mode.

request.name: set_desync
request.description: Change the commit behaviour of the sub-surface to desynchronized mode.
